newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece says Turkey must change stance to join EU.
newsitem.headline: Greece says Turkey must change stance to join EU.

text.p: Greece will help Turkey join the European family of nations if Ankara shows respect for international law and gives up its "visions of expansion", Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis said on Friday.
European Union member Greece has long been at odds with its eastern neighbour over a series of issues and has put up obstacles to closer Turkish relations with the 15-nation bloc.

"We want to help Turkey find its European orientation," Simitis said in a speech to his socialist party's central committee. "But first Turkey must give tangible proof that it will give up its visions of Ottoman expansion."

Greece's technocrat prime minister said Turkey can show its willingness to abide by European law and order by showing it respects the resolutions of international bodies regarding Greece and the divided island of Cyprus.

"Only then can Turkey expect help from Greece so that it will overcome underdevelopment, so that the Turkish people can make free and democratic choices within the extended European community," Simitis said.
But he made clear that Greece would continue to boost its defences and campaign internationally against Turkey as long as it perceived a threat from its fellow NATO member.
"Turkish aggression makes Greece the only European Union country which faces a threat to its national sovereignty," Simitis said.
Territorial rights in the Aegean Sea, minorities in both countries and the Mediterranean island of Cyprus are among a long list of subjects of dispute between Athens and Ankara.
The two countries almost clashed last January over a deserted islet in the eastern Aegean. War was averted by the last-minute intervention of the United States.
